notes: Runs the Local Branch Review Path against a fixture whose branch diff contains five deliberately planted defects, one per review angle (off-by-one, N+1 I/O, swallowed error, removed validation guard, altitude violation in a shared helper). Grading a review against known-planted bugs is what makes detection objectively checkable rather than a judgement call about whether the prose sounds thorough. gh is absent from PATH in every eval here, which is the condition the skill documents as 'no PR found for this branch' -- the PR Review Path needs live GitHub and is out of scope for an offline suite. Because `claude -p` cannot answer the skill's interactive prompts, each prompt pre-answers them the way a user would. Note on one flaky assertion: `no-pr-skip-line` greps for a line the skill prints mid-flow, but output.md holds only the agent's final message, so it passes or fails depending on whether that run restated the line in its summary. Judge it accordingly and prefer the state-based assertions around it.

evals.name: mode-selection-question
evals.expected_output: Before running any diff or analysis, the skill asks whether the user is reviewing a PR or their local working branch. With no answer forthcoming in a non-interactive session it may then default to the local branch and proceed, but the mode question must come first.

assertions.text: Asks whether the review target is a PR or the local working branch
The mode question is raised before any diff analysis or findings are presented

evals.name: local-branch-no-report
evals.prompt: Review my code on my local working branch. Please don't pause to triage findings with me one by one: treat every finding as 'later' (to be fixed) and work straight through all the review angles to the complete summary in one go. Don't generate a report file at the end.
evals.expected_output: The skill states it is starting a fresh local branch review, finds no open PR (gh is unavailable) and prints the skip line, runs the 7 review angles over the branch diff, and surfaces the planted defects. It triages every finding as 'To be fixed', prints a severity counts table and a What Looks Good section, and writes no report file. There is no Reviewer To-Do section because the PR and issue check never ran.

assertions.text: Prints the 'No PR found for this branch' skip line
assertions.script: grep -qi 'No PR found for this branch' output.md

assertions.text: Prints a severity counts table using the skill's severity levels
Findings carry the 'To be fixed' triage status the user asked for
Includes a What Looks Good section
Omits the Reviewer To-Do section entirely rather than printing an empty heading
Writes no report file under review/, since the user declined one
Flags the off-by-one loop bound in src/submissions.js, where i <= subs.length reads one element past the end
Flags the N+1 query: db.findOne is called once per submission inside the loop
Flags the empty catch block in createAssignment that swallows the insert failure and returns undefined
Flags that the title validation guard was removed from createAssignment
Flags the altitude problem: shared pageBounds now branches on a caller-specific callerContext value
Findings name a concrete failure (inputs leading to wrong output or a crash) rather than saying something could be a problem

evals.name: local-branch-with-report
evals.prompt: Review my code on my local working branch. Please don't pause to triage findings with me one by one: treat every finding as 'later' (to be fixed) and work straight through all the review angles to the complete summary in one go. Then yes, do generate the written report at the end.
evals.expected_output: As the no-report case, but after printing the summary the skill writes a report to review/<safe-branch>/report-<timestamp>.md containing the severity table, each finding's triage status, and the What Looks Good section, then prints the saved path.

assertions.text: Writes a report to review/<safe-branch>/report-<timestamp>.md
The report directory is the sanitised branch name feat-submission-listing, with the slash replaced
The report contains a severity counts table
The report records a triage status against findings
The report contains a What Looks Good section
assertions.script: find sandbox/review -name 'report-*.md' -exec grep -li 'what looks good' {} + | grep -q .

assertions.text: Prints the saved report path so the user can find it

evals.name: pr-check-skipped-cleanly
evals.prompt: Review my code on my local working branch. There's no PR open for this branch yet, I just want feedback before I push. Please don't pause to triage findings with me one by one: treat every finding as 'later' and go straight through to the complete summary. No report file at the end.
evals.expected_output: The PR and issue check resolves to no PR and is skipped in full: the skill does not go on to ask the reviewer for an issue number or evaluate a test plan, and produces no Reviewer To-Do section, because the check that generates those items never ran. The rest of the review proceeds normally.

assertions.text: Prints the 'No PR found for this branch' skip line
assertions.script: grep -qi 'No PR found for this branch' output.md

assertions.text: Does not go on to ask the reviewer to supply an issue number, since the whole check is skipped rather than run to completion
Produces no Reviewer To-Do section
The review itself still runs: a severity table and What Looks Good section are present
assertions.script: grep -q '🔴' output.md && grep -qi 'what looks good' output.md

evals.name: refuses-review-on-main
evals.prompt: Can you review my code changes on my local working branch please? Don't bother generating a report.
evals.expected_output: There are real uncommitted changes to review, but the current branch is main, which the skill treats as out of bounds: it stops immediately on the branch-name check and tells the user code reviews are for feature branches only, without producing findings, a severity table, or a report. The point of the eval is that the refusal is driven by the branch rule, not by an absence of anything to review, so it must not enumerate the defects sitting in the working tree.

assertions.text: Stops and states that code reviews are for feature branches only
The stated reason for stopping is that the current branch is a trunk branch, not that there is nothing to review
Produces no severity counts table, having stopped before the review angles
Does not review the uncommitted changes regardless: the off-by-one, N+1, and swallowed-error defects in the working tree go unenumerated
Writes no report file
Does not silently switch branches or commit the changes to make the review possible
assertions.script: test "$(git -C sandbox rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD)" = main && test -n "$(git -C sandbox status --porcelain)"
